- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment turns negative (≤-1.0) mid-history, model often overshoots downward; cap forecast decline at 5% below prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior), model frequently overcorrects downward; delay correction by 1–2 periods.
- If sentiment flips from positive to negative within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; apply mean reversion to 10–15% of prior range.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overpredicts early in the forecast window; apply 2–4% downward bias to first 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +1/-1 cycles, model tends to lag; add 1–2% lagged sentiment adjustment to forecast.
